items.review_rationale: Reviewed the I-adic inverse-limit construction for a Noetherian commutative ring, including ideal powers, quotient rings, transition maps, and its canonical structural map. The inverse-limit ring and completeness property are not interchangeable.

references.phrase: quotient ring R/I^n and ideal powers
references.context: Commutative algebra: successive ideal powers and ring quotient by the nth ideal power
Commutative algebra: compatible quotient maps induce universal ring homomorphism into inverse-limit ring

references.disposition: The inverse system uses the natural transition maps between ideal-power quotients and not arbitrary unrelated quotient rings.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the affine blowup chart as the degree-zero homogeneous localization of the Rees algebra at a chosen degree-one element represented by a∈I. Its fractions x/a^n have x∈I^n, not arbitrary numerator in R.

references.context: Commutative algebra: degree-zero fractions in homogeneous localization of graded Rees algebra

references.phrase: a chosen element of I in degree one
references.disposition: The element is represented in degree one; it is not assumed to be a unit or a nonzero divisor in R.

items.review_rationale: Read the full nonnegative grading with I⁰=R and pieces I^n and multiplication I^m I^n⊆I^{m+n}. Preserved the induced ring-algebra structure instead of identifying the Rees algebra with a simple quotient ring.

references.phrase: ideal I of commutative ring R

references.context: Commutative algebra: nth power of an ideal and multiplication of ideal powers
Algebra: external direct sum of an indexed family of modules with graded multiplication

references.disposition: The degree-zero component is the ambient ring; multiplication on homogeneous pieces comes from ideal multiplication.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed surjective local homomorphism B′→B, its kernel I of module length one, the square-zero consequence, and annihilation by the maximal ideal. A small extension is stronger than an arbitrary square-zero extension.

references.phrase: local Artinian rings B′ and B

references.context: Commutative algebra: surjective map of local rings respecting their unique maximal ideals
Ring theory: kernel of homomorphism as ideal of B′

references.phrase: I²=0 and maximal ideal annihilates I
references.disposition: These are mathematical consequences asserted of length-one kernel, not separate requirements equivalent for arbitrary extension.

items.review_rationale: Read the local lifting criterion over R Noetherian for finite-type R→S and prime q of S: lifts of compatible maps across all local R-algebra square-zero surjections. Preserve compatibility and location of q rather than generalizing to arbitrary extensions without the stated hypotheses.

references.phrase: formal smoothness lifting of ring map
square-zero kernel of local R-algebra surjection
references.context: Deformation theory: square-zero ideal kernel of surjective homomorphism of local R-algebras

references.phrase: compatibility of local lifting maps S→B′
references.context: Commutative algebra: commutative diagrams and lifts of R-algebra morphisms along a quotient map

references.phrase: maximal ideal of B lies over q
references.disposition: The displayed localization condition on target local algebra is part of the at-q test; it is not an arbitrary global lifting problem.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed pointwise construction F(X)×_{G(X)}H(X) of the fibre product presheaf with restriction maps inherited componentwise. This is a presheaf limit, not a scheme fibre product or a topological fibre product.

references.context: Category theory: natural transformations between contravariant set-valued functors

references.disposition: Functoriality of restrictions follows from the transformations' naturality and is not a distinct sheaf axiom.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the quantification over every U∈C and every element ξ∈G(U), the Yoneda map h_U→G, and the representability of its fibre product with F; a representable morphism need not make F or G representable itself.

references.context: Category theory: natural transformation of contravariant set-valued functors

references.phrase: ξ∈G(U) as Yoneda natural transformation h_U→G
references.context: Category theory: Yoneda correspondence between elements of presheaf G(U) and natural transformations from h_U

references.disposition: Representability is tested on every such pullback, not only on a fixed single object or one chosen element.

items.review_rationale: Read the Jacobson-space condition as the density in each closed subset Z of those points that are closed in the entire ambient space X; this is not the weaker statement that points closed only relatively in Z are dense.

references.context: Topology: singleton {x} closed in the original space X, distinguished from closure relative to Z

references.phrase: for each closed Z the ambient closed points in Z are dense
references.disposition: The quantifier ranges over every closed subset including X; the closure is taken within Z.
